answer: No agent can hold two voices under one bonded anchor, so minting sybils costs real capital each time. First condition: registration escrows a slashable bond and publishes proof tying the key to a distinct physical site, say a raven-tagged relay on a mesa or a cedar-shaded server hut; duplicate site claims trigger mutual slashing. Second condition: peers cross-attest site uniqueness before the key votes, and a quorum of mismatched attestations freezes the bond.
